_about: HomeKeeper rule base for the Allegheny County pre-1960 single-family pilot. Each rule cites one primary source (data/sources.json) and states what that source supports. review_status 'author-reviewed' means the recommendation was checked against the cited source during the Checkpoint 1 audit; it is NOT independent expert validation (Checkpoint 9 benchmark). Intervals that no primary source states are labelled planning_assumption in the recurrence.

rules.title: Test smoke and CO alarms monthly; record manufacture dates
rules.action: Press the test button on every smoke and CO alarm. On first pass, write down the manufacture date printed on the back of each unit; replace batteries at least yearly.
rules.why: Applies to every home. CPSC: test monthly, replace batteries at least annually.
rules.safe_observation: Test button only; do not open sealed units.
rules.delay_consequence: A dead alarm gives no warning; CPSC links most fatal fires to missing or non-working alarms (statement from Pub 559).
rules.priority_rationale: Life safety; trivial effort; no cost.
rules.completion_criteria: Every alarm sounded on test; dates recorded in the house record.
rules.retain_evidence: Alarm manufacture dates (photo of back label).
rules.source_ref: CPSC Pub 559 'Smoke Alarms – Why, Where, and Which': test once a month; replace batteries at least annually

rules.title: Replace smoke alarms older than 10 years; CO alarms per their label
rules.verification_task: Read the manufacture date on the back of each smoke and CO alarm and record the oldest year.
rules.action: Replace any smoke alarm manufactured more than 10 years ago; replace CO alarms at the age printed on the unit. Prefer interconnected units with sealed 10-year batteries.
rules.why: CPSC: replace smoke alarms that are more than 10 years old; CO alarms have a manufacturer replacement age.
rules.delay_consequence: Sensors degrade; an old alarm can pass a button test and still fail to detect smoke.
rules.completion_criteria: No alarm older than 10 years in the record.
rules.source_ref: CPSC Pub 559: replace smoke alarms more than 10 years old; CPSC CO Fact Sheet: alarms have a recommended replacement age

rules.title: Test GFCI outlets and breakers monthly
rules.action: Press TEST then RESET on every GFCI receptacle and GFCI breaker (kitchen, baths, basement, garage, exterior). Any that does not trip or reset needs replacement.
rules.why: CPSC: test every GFCI at least once a month, after installation and after power failures.
rules.delay_consequence: A failed GFCI leaves wet-area circuits without shock protection.
rules.completion_criteria: All GFCIs tripped and reset.
rules.retain_evidence: Note any failed device and its location.
rules.source_ref: CPSC Pub 099 'What Is A GFCI?': test at least once a month; Pub 513 Home Electrical Safety Checklist

rules.title: Establish the wiring type and grounding (pre-1960 house)
rules.verification_task: Check the inspection report's electrical section for knob-and-tube, ungrounded two-slot receptacles, aluminum branch wiring or an undersized panel. Record what it says. If the report is silent, ask an electrician to assess.
rules.action: Have a licensed electrician assess and quote remediation; CPSC notes GFCI receptacles may replace ungrounded two-slot receptacles (labelled 'No Equipment Ground').
rules.why: Houses of this era commonly retain original wiring; the assessor record says nothing about it and the inspection report is the only document that does.
rules.pro_conditions: Any knob-and-tube, scorching, double-tapped breakers or missing grounds — professional only.
rules.delay_consequence: Fire and shock risk is unquantified until assessed; insurers may ask about knob-and-tube.
rules.effort: 15 minutes to read the report; assessment visit if needed
rules.priority_rationale: Safety; evidence usually already exists in the inspection report.
rules.completion_criteria: wiring_type recorded with the report page or electrician's note as source.
rules.retain_evidence: Inspection report electrical pages; electrician's assessment.
rules.source_ref: CPSC Pub 099: GFCI receptacles may replace ungrounded two-slot receptacles with a 'NO EQUIPMENT GROUND' label; InterNACHI SOP §3 electrical scope

rules.title: Annual professional inspection and service of the fuel-burning heating system
rules.action: Before the heating season, have a heating professional inspect and service the furnace or boiler: vent connector and chimney/flue, heat exchanger, combustion/CO check, blower or circulator, controls. Ask for the CO reading in writing.
rules.why: Fuel-burning heating equipment produces combustion gases; CPSC recommends professional inspection every year.
rules.pro_conditions: All of it — combustion equipment is professional work.
rules.delay_consequence: Carbon-monoxide exposure risk and mid-winter failure; many manufacturer warranties condition coverage on maintenance.
rules.completion_criteria: Service invoice with date, CO reading and technician notes in the house record.
rules.retain_evidence: Invoice; CO reading; any parts replaced.

cost.note: No free local price source; enter your quote.

goodman_rs6612023.note: Goodman RS6612023r2: furnace inspected at least once per year by a qualified servicer

carrier_58d_u_9sm.note: Carrier 58D,U-9SM: blower and electrical service annually by a qualified technician

rules.source_ref: CPSC NSN-9 'Inspect, Detect and Protect': have a professional inspect all fuel-burning heating systems every year; DOE Energy Saver furnace/boiler checklist

rules.title: Check the furnace/air-handler filter
rules.action: Check the filter; replace when dirty. Without a manufacturer instruction, check monthly during heating and cooling seasons (DOE's AC guidance) and record the filter size.
rules.why: A clogged filter restricts airflow; DOE recommends monthly checks in season. Your furnace manual's own interval overrides this when known.
rules.delay_consequence: Higher bills, reduced heat, and strain on the blower and heat exchanger.

recurrence.basis: DOE AC guidance applied to forced-air heating; manufacturer interval preferred

rules.priority_rationale: Cheap, frequent, protects the most expensive system.
rules.completion_criteria: Filter checked/replaced; size and date recorded.

goodman_rs6612023.action: Clean or replace the filter every two months or as required (Goodman).
goodman_rs6612023.note: Goodman RS6612023r2: filters cleaned/replaced every two months or as required

carrier_58d_u_9sm.action: Check and clean the air filter each month, more often if required (Carrier).
carrier_58d_u_9sm.note: Carrier 58D,U-9SM: check and clean air filter each month or more frequently if required

rules.source_ref: DOE Energy Saver 'Maintaining Your Air Conditioner': clean or replace filters every month or two in season (applied to forced-air heating as a planning assumption)

rules.title: Boiler: test the pressure-relief valve and check the expansion tank at annual service
rules.action: Ask the technician at the annual service to test the pressure-relief valve and high-limit control, check the expansion tank (hot-water) or drain sediment and test the low-water cutoff (steam).
rules.why: DOE's professional maintenance checklist for hot-water and steam systems names these items.
rules.delay_consequence: A stuck relief valve or failed low-water cutoff is a safety failure, not just a comfort one.
rules.completion_criteria: Service invoice lists relief valve/limit/low-water cutoff checked.
rules.source_ref: DOE Energy Saver 'Furnaces and Boilers': hot-water systems — test pressure-relief valve, high-limit control, expansion tank; steam — drain sediment, test low-water cutoff

rules.title: Central AC: filter monthly in season, clear the outdoor unit, annual coil check
rules.action: Clean or replace the filter every month or two during cooling season; keep about 2 ft clear around the outdoor condenser and remove debris; have the evaporator coil checked yearly and the drain channels cleared.
rules.why: DOE Energy Saver AC maintenance guidance.
rules.pro_conditions: Refrigerant, electrical and coil cleaning inside the cabinet — professional.
rules.delay_consequence: Reduced cooling, higher bills, frozen coil.
rules.completion_criteria: Pre-season check recorded; service invoice if a pro visited.
rules.source_ref: DOE Energy Saver 'Maintaining Your Air Conditioner': filter every month or two; evaporator coil every year; keep ~2 ft clearance; clear drain channels

rules.title: Water heater: test the T&P relief valve, flush sediment, check the anode
rules.action: Lift the T&P relief valve lever briefly and confirm it reseats (yearly per Bradford White and A. O. Smith; every 6 months per DOE). Drain sediment (DOE: a quart every 3 months; Bradford White: a gallon monthly; A. O. Smith: flush after 6 months). Have the anode rod inspected (A. O. Smith: annually after 6 months; DOE: every 3–4 years). Set the thermostat near 120°F unless you have a reason for hotter.
rules.why: Manufacturer manuals and DOE agree on the tasks; they differ on intervals, so the range and its sources are shown. Your heater's manual overrides when identified.
rules.safe_observation: T&P test discharges hot water — ensure the discharge pipe ends somewhere safe before lifting the lever.
rules.pro_conditions: A T&P valve that drips afterwards or won't reseat; gas-valve or venting issues; anode replacement if seized.
rules.delay_consequence: Sediment shortens tank life and a stuck T&P valve removes the tank's over-pressure protection.

recurrence.basis: annual T&P/anode per manufacturer manuals; DOE gives shorter sediment interval

rules.completion_criteria: T&P tested, sediment drained, anode checked; dates recorded.
rules.retain_evidence: Model and serial (label photo); anode condition note.

cost.note: Anode replacement cost unknown until quoted.

bradford_white_io.action: Check the T&P relief valve at least once a year; drain a gallon monthly for sediment; inspect the anode periodically; have the vent inspected yearly (Bradford White I&O).

aosmith_100398943.action: Inspect and operate the T&P valve annually; inspect the anode at 6 months then at least annually; flush after the first six months (A. O. Smith).

rules.source_ref: DOE Energy Saver 'Storage Water Heaters': flush a quart every three months; check T&P every six months; inspect anode every three to four years; ~120°F

rules.title: Plan a water-heater replacement window
rules.action: Start a replacement reserve; watch for rust at the base, moisture, or inconsistent hot water. This is planning, not a prediction — units often outlast the estimate.
rules.why: InterNACHI estimates 6–12 years for conventional tank heaters (NAHB 2007: 10); a unit at 8+ years is in its planning window.
rules.delay_consequence: Emergency replacement at the worst price, and a leaking tank in a basement.
rules.completion_criteria: Reserve scenario chosen in the future-replacements budget.

cost.note: Enter a quote or choose a planning range.

rules.source_ref: InterNACHI life-expectancy chart: conventional water heater 6–12 years (guideline only); NAHB 2007 study: gas water heater 10 years

rules.title: Register new equipment with the manufacturer before the deadline
rules.action: Register the new unit on the manufacturer's site within its deadline (Goodman: 60 days; Carrier: 90 days) and file the confirmation; unregistered units typically drop to the shorter base warranty.
rules.why: Manufacturer warranty terms condition the longer parts warranty on timely registration.
rules.delay_consequence: Loss of the extended parts warranty (e.g., 10-year vs 5-year).
rules.priority_rationale: Hard deadline with a large warranty consequence.
rules.completion_criteria: Registration confirmation stored with the equipment record.
rules.retain_evidence: Registration confirmation; installer invoice; serial number.
rules.source_ref: Goodman Warranty Overview PM-WARRCHRT-G: online registration within 60 days of installation; Carrier warranty page: 90 days to register

rules.title: Annual chimney and flue inspection (Level 1)
rules.action: Arrange a Level 1 chimney inspection before the heating season; sweep if 1/8 inch of soot has built up. Ask whether the flue is lined and whether the heating appliance vents through it.
rules.why: The record lists a fireplace. CSIA (citing NFPA 211) recommends annual inspection; CPSC includes chimneys and flues in its CO guidance.
rules.delay_consequence: Flue blockage or liner failure can vent CO into the house or start a chimney fire.
rules.priority_rationale: Fire/CO risk; pre-1960 masonry chimneys are often unlined.
rules.completion_criteria: Inspection report in the house record.
rules.source_ref: CSIA Homeowner Resources: chimneys inspected at least once a year (NFPA 211); sweep at 1/8 in buildup; CPSC CO Fact Sheet: check chimneys and flues

rules.title: Establish the roof's installation date
rules.action: Ask the seller/agent for roofing paperwork, read the inspection report's roof section, and check permit history (City of Pittsburgh parcels). Record the year with its source.
rules.why: Replacement planning is provisional until the roof's age and condition are established; inspectors are not required to predict roof life.
rules.delay_consequence: The largest replacement cost in this housing stock stays unplanned.
rules.completion_criteria: roof_installed_year recorded with a source.
rules.source_ref: InterNACHI SOP §3.1: inspector not required to predict roof service life; §2.1.08 life expectancy not determined

rules.title: Plan an asphalt-roof replacement window
rules.action: Start a replacement reserve and get a roofer's condition assessment at the next seasonal check; condition drives timing more than age.
rules.why: InterNACHI estimates 20 years (3-tab) to 30 (architectural) for asphalt shingles; a roof past 15 years is in its planning window.
rules.delay_consequence: Unplanned replacement; water damage if deferred past failure.
rules.completion_criteria: Reserve scenario chosen.
rules.source_ref: InterNACHI chart: asphalt 3-tab 20 yr / architectural 30 yr (guideline only); NAHB 2007: asphalt shingles ~20 yr

rules.title: Seasonal roof and flashing visual check (spring and fall, and after severe weather)
rules.action: From the ground or a window, look for missing/lifted shingles, exposed nails, rust at flashings, debris in valleys, and daylight or staining in the attic. Do not walk the roof.
rules.why: NRCA recommends scheduled roof inspections at least twice a year plus after severe weather (reported by Professional Roofing).
rules.safe_observation: Ground level with binoculars or a camera; attic check with a flashlight.
rules.pro_conditions: Anything you see that needs a ladder on a slope, or any active leak.
rules.delay_consequence: Small flashing leaks become sheathing and ceiling damage.
rules.completion_criteria: Check recorded with any observations and photos.
rules.source_ref: Professional Roofing article 4787 reporting NRCA's recommendation of roof inspections at least twice per year (spring/fall) and after severe weather

rules.title: Clean gutters and confirm downspouts discharge 5–10 ft from the foundation
rules.action: Clear gutters and downspout outlets; confirm every downspout carries water at least 5–10 ft from the house (extensions or splash blocks). EPA says clean and repair gutters regularly; the twice-yearly cadence (after leaf fall, after spring) is a planning assumption, not a sourced interval.
rules.why: Roof runoff dumped at the foundation is the most common driver of basement water in this housing stock; ISU Extension gives the 5–10 ft figure.
rules.safe_observation: Watch during a rain; look for overflow and splash at the base of the wall.
rules.pro_conditions: Two-story gutters or steep ground — hire it out.
rules.delay_consequence: Basement seepage, efflorescence, and foundation moisture.
rules.completion_criteria: Gutters clear; every downspout discharging 5–10 ft away; recorded.
rules.source_ref: ISU Extension Pm-1560: downspouts should discharge at least 5 to 10 feet from the house; EPA Mold Guide p.10: clean and repair roof gutters regularly

rules.title: Check that the ground slopes away from the foundation
rules.action: Walk the perimeter after a rain: the first 10 ft should drop about 6 in away from the house (ISU Extension). Note low spots, settled backfill, window wells that hold water, and paving that slopes toward the wall.
rules.why: Houses with below-grade space depend on surface drainage; EPA and ISU Extension both call for ground sloping away from the foundation.
rules.pro_conditions: Regrading against a foundation wall, or any sign of movement/cracking — professional.
rules.delay_consequence: Water against the wall; seepage; freeze–thaw damage.
rules.priority_rationale: Cheap check with a large downstream effect.
rules.completion_criteria: Grading observation recorded; any low spots photographed.
rules.source_ref: ISU Extension Pm-1560: first 10 ft from the house should drop at least 6 in; EPA Mold Guide p.10: ground slopes away from the building foundation

rules.title: Keep basement humidity below 60% and dry any wet spot within 24–48 hours
rules.action: Put an inexpensive hygrometer in the basement; run a dehumidifier in humid months to keep relative humidity under 60% (ideally 30–50%). Dry any wet material within 24–48 hours; cleanup larger than about 10 sq ft of mold warrants professional help.
rules.why: EPA mold guidance thresholds; old basements in this climate run humid all summer.
rules.delay_consequence: Mold growth, musty odors, and damage to stored items and finishes.
rules.priority_rationale: Health and material damage; cheap control.
rules.completion_criteria: Hygrometer in place; readings under 60% during humid months.
rules.source_ref: EPA 'A Brief Guide to Mold, Moisture and Your Home' pp.3,4,10,11: humidity below 60%; dry within 24–48 h; DIY cleanup under ~10 sq ft

rules.title: Test the sump pump
rules.verification_task: Check the basement for a sump pit and pump; record whether one is present, and photograph the pump label if so.
rules.action: Pour water into the pit until the float rises; confirm the pump runs, empties the pit, the check valve holds and the discharge runs clear outside. Clear debris from the pit. Without a manufacturer instruction, test quarterly (planning assumption aligned with Zoeller's interval).
rules.why: A basement home with a sump pump depends on it in wet weather; manufacturer instructions call for periodic testing.
rules.safe_observation: Keep hands clear of the impeller; unplug before clearing debris.
rules.pro_conditions: Pump doesn't run, runs constantly, or trips the GFCI.
rules.delay_consequence: A silent pump failure is discovered during the storm that floods the basement.
rules.priority_rationale: Basement water is the dominant risk in this housing stock.
rules.completion_criteria: Pump cycled on test; date recorded.
rules.retain_evidence: Pump label photo (make/model) for its manual.

zoeller_fm2676.action: Inspect and test the system at least every three months; check frequently for debris (Zoeller FM2676).
zoeller_fm2676.source_ref: FM2676 maintenance section; 3-year warranty void if not maintained per instructions

liberty_7035000.action: Monthly: run the pump and check operation; quarterly checks; annually inspect and clean the basin and replace defective components (Liberty 7035000).

rules.source_ref: Zoeller FM2676: inspect and test for proper operation at least every three months (used as the generic planning interval until the installed model is identified)

rules.title: Plan a sump-pump replacement and consider battery backup
rules.action: Budget a replacement; consider a battery backup or water-powered backup if the basement is finished or storms coincide with outages.
rules.why: InterNACHI estimates about 7 years for sump pumps; a pump at 6+ years is in its window.
rules.delay_consequence: Failure during a storm.
rules.completion_criteria: Reserve chosen; backup decision recorded.
rules.source_ref: InterNACHI chart: sump pump 7 years (guideline only)

rules.title: Test for radon (or file a result from the last two years)
rules.action: Run a short-term test on the lowest lived-in level, or file the inspection's radon result in the house record. At 4 pCi/L or above, get mitigation quotes; EPA says consider fixing between 2 and 4.
rules.why: EPA recommends testing every home below the third floor; PA law requires only disclosure at sale, not a test.
rules.delay_consequence: Unmeasured exposure; the seller-remediation window closes at closing.
rules.priority_rationale: Health exposure; cheap to measure; transaction window.
rules.completion_criteria: Result (pCi/L, date, floor) stored in the house record.

cost.note: Test kits are inexpensive; mitigation unknown until quoted.

rules.source_ref: EPA Citizen's Guide to Radon pp.2–3, 10, 12: test homes below third floor; fix at 4 pCi/L; consider 2–4; retest every two years

rules.title: Radon at or above 4 pCi/L: get mitigation quotes
rules.action: Get quotes from PA DEP-certified mitigators; after installation, test within 30 days (not sooner than 24 h after startup) and then at least every two years.
rules.why: EPA action level is 4 pCi/L; the recorded result is at or above it.
rules.delay_consequence: Continued exposure at a level EPA says to fix.
rules.priority_rationale: Measured exposure above the action level.
rules.completion_criteria: System installed; post-mitigation test result filed.

cost.note: DEP's mitigation dataset (vm4e-6nir) can show reported system costs for context.

rules.source_ref: EPA Consumer's Guide to Radon Reduction p.13: post-mitigation test within 30 days, not sooner than 24 h after startup; retest at least every two years; Citizen's Guide p.2: fix at 4 pCi/L or higher

rules.title: Radon mitigation system: check the manometer and plan for fan replacement
rules.action: Glance at the U-tube manometer on the pipe (unequal liquid levels mean the fan is pulling); retest every two years; budget a fan replacement — EPA says fans may last five years or more.
rules.why: EPA mitigation-system upkeep guidance.
rules.delay_consequence: A dead fan silently returns the house to its pre-mitigation level.
rules.completion_criteria: Manometer checked; retest on the two-year cycle.
rules.source_ref: EPA Consumer's Guide to Radon Reduction p.13: check manometer regularly; retest at least every two years; fans may last five years or more

rules.title: Lead-based paint: collect the disclosure and pamphlet; assess if children will live here
rules.action: Confirm you received the seller's lead-based-paint disclosure and the EPA pamphlet; if children under six will live in the home, use the 10-day window for a lead inspection or risk assessment, and plan lead-safe practices for any renovation.
rules.why: Built before 1978: federal lead disclosure rules apply.
rules.delay_consequence: Loss of the pre-closing inspection window; exposure risk during renovation.
rules.completion_criteria: Disclosure and pamphlet filed; assessment decision recorded.
rules.source_ref: EPA real-estate disclosure page (Section 1018, Title X): pre-1978 housing — pamphlet, disclosure, 10-day inspection opportunity

rules.title: Clean the dryer vent duct; replace any plastic or foil duct with metal
rules.action: Clean the lint screen every load; periodically disconnect and clean the exhaust duct and the outside hood; replace plastic or foil accordion duct with rigid or semi-rigid metal. The yearly duct cleaning cadence is a planning assumption (CPSC says 'periodically').
rules.why: CPSC dryer-fire guidance.
rules.pro_conditions: Long or inaccessible duct runs; gas dryer connections.
rules.delay_consequence: Lint fires; long dry times.
rules.completion_criteria: Duct cleaned; duct material recorded.
rules.source_ref: CPSC Pub 5022 'Overheated Clothes Dryers Can Cause Fires': clean lint screen each load; clean vent and exhaust duct periodically; use rigid or semi-rigid metal duct

rules.title: Winterize exterior hose bibs before the first freeze
rules.action: Disconnect hoses, close any interior shutoff for each exterior faucet and open the exterior valve to drain it; for frost-free faucets, disconnecting the hose is the essential step.
rules.why: Pittsburgh's median first 32°F date is about October 20 (NCEI normals); freeze-split pipes behind a wall are a common winter loss. The task is standard practice; the timing is sourced, the practice is a planning assumption.
rules.delay_consequence: A split pipe that floods a wall or basement during the first hard freeze.

recurrence.basis: NCEI 1991–2020 median first freeze Oct 20 at USW00094823

rules.completion_criteria: Hoses off; valves drained; date recorded.
rules.source_ref: NCEI 1991–2020 normals, station USW00094823: ANN-TMIN-PRBFST-T32FP50 = 10/20 (50% probability first 32°F)

rules.title: Flood zone: check insurance status and basement water history
rules.action: Confirm with lender and insurer whether flood insurance is required or advisable; ask the seller disclosure (item 4, basements) about water entry; check for a LOMA for the property.
rules.why: FEMA's flood hazard layer places this point inside a Special Flood Hazard Area.
rules.delay_consequence: Insurance decisions are tied to closing; uninsured flood loss.
rules.completion_criteria: Insurance decision and any LOMA recorded.
rules.source_ref: NFHL layer 28 SFHA_TF = T at the geocoded point; LOMA layer 2 to be checked

rules.title: Consider Mine Subsidence Insurance before closing
rules.action: Look up the address on PA DEP's Mine Subsidence Insurance map and decide on coverage; a policy applied for at purchase agreement takes effect at closing. Homeowners policies usually exclude subsidence.
rules.why: DEP's confirmed-mining layer intersects this point (a flag only; not a parcel-level mine-map review).
rules.delay_consequence: Uninsured subsidence damage; coverage timing tied to closing.
rules.priority_rationale: Coverage decision tied to the closing date.
rules.completion_criteria: Decision recorded (policy number or 'declined').

cost.note: DEP FAQ cites roughly $0.27 per $1,000 of coverage; confirm current rate.

rules.source_ref: DEP MSI confirmed-mining layer point intersect; DEP MSI FAQ (coverage effective at closing when applied for at purchase agreement)

rules.title: Landslide-prone area: review retaining walls, slope and drainage with the inspection report
rules.action: Read the inspection report's site/retaining-wall notes; look for leaning or bulging walls, tension cracks, trees leaning downhill, and downspouts discharging onto the slope. If anything is noted, get a geotechnical or structural assessment before closing.
rules.why: The county's landslide-prone layer intersects this point; drainage onto a slope is the controllable factor.
rules.pro_conditions: Any wall movement or slope cracking — professional.
rules.delay_consequence: Slope or wall failure is expensive and often uninsured.
rules.priority_rationale: Regional exposure that the inspection can confirm or clear.
rules.completion_criteria: Observation recorded; assessment if warranted.
rules.source_ref: PASDA Allegheny County Landslide Prone 202509 point intersect (City of Pittsburgh extent)

rules.title: Poorly drained or high water-table soil map unit: pay extra attention to basement water evidence
rules.action: Treat basement water evidence in the inspection report (staining, efflorescence, sump activity) as likely recurring; prioritise the gutter, grading and sump tasks and ask the seller disclosure about water entry.
rules.why: The mapped soil unit's natural drainage class is poor; this describes the area, not the lot, and does not establish the foundation's condition.
rules.delay_consequence: Recurring seepage treated as a one-off.
rules.priority_rationale: Raises the weight of other evidence; no cost.
rules.completion_criteria: Noted against the basement tasks.
rules.source_ref: SSURGO component.drainagecl for the map unit at the point; NRCS: map units do not replace on-site investigation

rules.title: Point-of-sale sewer dye test / lateral certification
rules.verification_task: Ask the municipality (or the agent) whether a point-of-sale sewer dye test or lateral inspection is required; no entry is compiled for this municipality yet.
rules.action: Confirm the municipality's dye test (and lateral camera inspection where required) is scheduled far enough before closing; ask for the certificate and any repair records for the house record.
rules.why: The municipality requires a sewer certification before sale; lead times run 7–30 days and a failed test can require repairs before closing.
rules.delay_consequence: Closing delay or seller-side repair dispute.
rules.completion_criteria: Certificate stored in the house record.

cost.note: Municipal fee per the compiled table; plumber charge unknown.

rules.source_ref: data/municipal_dye_tests.json entry for the municipality (primary municipal page/code cited there)

rules.title: Private sewer lateral: establish material and condition (pre-1960 house)
rules.action: If the municipality's sale process did not include a camera inspection of the lateral, consider one before closing or in the first year; record the material (clay, cast iron, Orangeburg) and any root intrusion.
rules.why: Laterals of this era are commonly clay or cast iron; the homeowner owns the lateral to the main in most Allegheny County municipalities (ALCOSAN: municipalities own local sewers; private laterals are the owner's).
rules.delay_consequence: Sewer backup into the basement; emergency excavation.
rules.completion_criteria: Lateral material and condition recorded with the video/report.
rules.source_ref: Municipal dye-test/lateral programs (Upper St. Clair, Bethel Park, Dormont, Baldwin require lateral video at sale); ALCOSAN municipal-customers page on sewer ownership

rules.title: Establish supply and drain pipe materials (galvanized, cast iron, copper, lead)
rules.verification_task: Read the inspection report's plumbing section and look at exposed pipes in the basement: grey threaded pipe is galvanized steel; black heavy pipe is cast iron; a dull grey soft pipe at the meter may be lead. Record what you find.
rules.action: Galvanized supply piping is near or past InterNACHI's estimated life and often restricts flow; plan a repipe quote. For PWSA customers, check the lead service line inventory and request a free replacement if the private side is lead or unknown.
rules.why: The assessor record never records pipe materials; houses of this era commonly retain original galvanized supply and cast-iron drains.
rules.delay_consequence: Low pressure, leaks inside walls, and (for lead) a health exposure.
rules.priority_rationale: Lead possibility raises this from budget to health.
rules.completion_criteria: Materials recorded with source.
rules.retain_evidence: Photos of pipe at the meter and main stack.
rules.source_ref: InterNACHI chart: galvanized/copper water lines and cast-iron waste pipe estimated lives (guideline only); PWSA lead service line program page

rules.title: Wood-destroying insect inspection and moisture contact at wood
rules.action: If the purchase did not include a wood-destroying insect (WDI) inspection, get one; keep soil and mulch below sill plates and wood siding, and fix wood-to-ground contact.
rules.why: Allegheny County municipalities adopt the IRC termite probability 'moderate to heavy' (e.g., Shaler Township UCC ordinance); the seller disclosure form asks about infestation (item 5).
rules.delay_consequence: Hidden structural damage.
rules.priority_rationale: Regional exposure that only an inspection can resolve.
rules.completion_criteria: WDI report filed; wdi_inspection_date recorded.
rules.source_ref: Shaler Township UCC ordinance: Termite 'Moderate to heavy'; PA seller disclosure form item 5 (termites/wood-destroying insects)

rules.title: Before you buy: reconcile the seller disclosure with the inspection report
rules.action: Read the seller's property disclosure statement (PA law lists roof, basements, structure, water/sewage, plumbing, heating/AC, electrical, soils/drainage, hazardous substances) against the inspection findings; list every 'yes/unknown' answer and every report finding that the other document does not mention. Those are your questions before the inspection contingency expires.
rules.why: PA's Real Estate Seller Disclosure Law defines what the seller must disclose; the inspection report is the independent evidence.
rules.delay_consequence: Lost contingency leverage.
rules.completion_criteria: Question list sent to the agent; answers filed.
rules.source_ref: 68 Pa.C.S. §7304(b) subjects of disclosure; form at 49 Pa. Code §35.335a

rules.title: Major work needs a municipal permit under the PA Uniform Construction Code
rules.action: Before structural, electrical, plumbing, HVAC replacement or roofing work, ask the municipality's building office what permits apply; plumbing permits in Allegheny County come from the Health Department and must be pulled by a registered master plumber (or owner-occupant).
rules.why: PA enforces the UCC through municipalities (2021 I-Codes effective 2026-01-01 per L&I); unpermitted work surfaces at the next sale.
rules.delay_consequence: Failed sale certifications; insurance disputes.
rules.completion_criteria: Permit numbers filed with the project record.
rules.source_ref: PA L&I UCC page (Triennial Update effective 2026-01-01); ACHD Plumbing Program (permits pulled by registered master plumbers)

rules.title: Seal obvious air leaks at windows, doors and the sill (optional improvement)
rules.action: Caulk gaps at window and door trim and the foundation sill with latex or silicone caulk; leave duct sealing to a contractor. Do this after moisture problems are controlled, not before.
rules.why: DOE air-sealing guidance; optional comfort/energy improvement, deliberately ranked last.
rules.delay_consequence: Higher heating bills; no safety consequence.
rules.priority_rationale: Optional; never outranks safety or water tasks.
rules.completion_criteria: Done; noted.
rules.source_ref: DOE Energy Saver 'Seal Air Leaks with Caulk': caulk windows/doors/foundation sill; leave duct sealing to a contractor
